utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon. This is IT-97-24-A, the Prosecutor versus Mr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, registrar. Can I please have the appearances of the parties. First the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon, counsel for Mr. Stakic. Appearing for the Prosecution is Norman Farrell, Mr. Xavier Tracol, and Susan Grogan. I've asked Mr. Tracol to deal with any issues that might arise in the Status Conference, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Farrell. Appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. John Ostojic and Branko Lukic on behalf of Mr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Stakic, can you hear me and understand me in a language that you understand? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Yes, I can hear and understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: This is a Status Conference called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis (B) requires that a Status Conference be convened within 120 days of the last Status Conference to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. Our last Status Conference in this case was on 5 April 2004. Mr. Stakic, let me address you again. Do you have any issues to raise in relation to your detention? Do you have any concerns regarding your mental or physical well-being that you would like to raise with me? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you for your concern, Your Honour. I have nothing new to report at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stakic. I'm not aware of any special matters outstanding in this appeal, and I would like merely to remind counsel for the Prosecution that under the Appeals Chamber decision on the motion to disallow the 20th of July, they have ten days from the decision of that motion to file an addendum to their response brief. Counsel for the accused then have ten days after that to file an addendum to their reply brief. Both addenda should be closely to the subject matter and page limitations set out in the decision of the 20th of July. Do either of the parties wish to raise any other issues at this time? Defence? Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I think you would have no difficulty in rendering this very long statement you made in English. May I suggest that you do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRACOL
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. I was not aware that there was no interpretation from French into English. I was just saying that the Prosecution filed its addendum on the 22nd of July, as requested by the Appeals Chamber, although we had the deadline on the 30th of July, 2004.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We probably will be able to do it without interpretation in the future, given the financial freeze and all of that. I take it that no one would like to raise any additional issues. And as there are no other issues, I would like simply to thank the parties for their attendance today and call the proceedings to a close. Thank you.
